title: Carrot Cake
subtitle: a spiced, oil-based cake with cream cheese frosting
excerpt: Carrot cake is moist, warmly spiced, and keeps well for several days. Oil replaces butter in the batter, which keeps the crumb tender even when cold. The cream cheese frosting is sharp and rich against the sweet, spiced cake.
sourceNotes: Carrot cake became popular in Britain in the 1960s and 70s, adopted partly from American and Swiss baking traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfrosted. Defrost and frost on the day of serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and frost on the day. The cake improves overnight.

content.text: Grate the carrots on the coarse side of the grater. Do not squeeze out any liquid -- the moisture is part of what makes the cake tender. This is a one-bowl batter that comes together quickly.

items.prepNote: use 200g full-fat cream cheese for frosting

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Grease and line two 20cm round tins. Coarsely grate about 300g of peeled carrots (roughly 3 large carrots).
Whisk together the oil, both sugars, and eggs until combined. Sift in the flour, baking powder, bicarb, and spices. Fold together. Stir in the grated carrot.
Divide between the two tins. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out.
For the frosting: beat the cream cheese and softened butter together. Sift in the icing sugar and beat until smooth and spreadable.
Sandwich the cooled layers with half the frosting. Spread the rest over the top. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: Batter over-mixed once the flour was added.
items.fix: Fold the dry ingredients in gently. Stop as soon as the flour disappears.

items.symptom: Frosting is too runny to spread
items.fix: Refrigerate the frosting for 20 minutes before spreading. Cold cream cheese frosting is much easier to work with.

content.text: Carrot cake became fashionable in Britain during the 1970s, partly because it was marketed as a healthier option. The cream cheese frosting is an American addition. Today it appears in virtually every British cafe and is one of the bestselling cakes in the country. It keeps better than most cakes and is excellent for several days after baking.
